# CC0 / Public-Domain Art Reference Kit  
## Hands, Poses, Turnarounds, Secondary Motion & Interiors

A curated, quality-first set of CC0 and public-domain resources for drawing hands and poses, building character side/back views and turnarounds, animating cloth and flags, and designing interiors.

---

## How to use this kit

1. **Use hand and pose references** to establish believable gesture, weight, and anatomy.
2. **Use turnaround sheets** to keep a character consistent across front, side, back, and three-quarter views.
3. **Use flag and cloth references** to learn secondary motion: follow-through, overlap, drag, and timing.
4. **Use interior tilesets and references** to design readable rooms, furniture, lighting, and space.
5. **Study at multiple scales:** gesture first, then construction, then pixel-level rendering.

### Hand study workflow

1. Start with a simple **mitten shape** to establish overall gesture.
2. Add the palm mass, thumb base, and finger direction.
3. Separate fingers only after the gesture reads clearly.
4. Add knuckles, creases, nails, and shading last.
5. For pixel art, reduce the hand to 3–7 readable shapes before adding detail.

### Pose study targets

- Standing, walking, running, sitting, crouching, and reaching
- Weight distribution and balance line
- Foreshortening in arms, legs, and hands
- Action poses: combat, casting, climbing, carrying, and falling
- Character-specific posture: confident, injured, sneaky, exhausted, or regal

## Character side and back views

| Resource | Best for | License / status |
|---|---|---|
| [OpenGameArt — Cartoon Male Turnaround and Walk Cycle Sheet](https://opengameart.org/content/cartoon-male-turn-around-and-walk-cycle-sheet) | A complete CC0 character turnaround with front, three-quarter, side, and back views, plus a walk cycle. | CC0 |
| [OpenGameArt — Pixel Art Character](https://opengameart.org/content/pixel-art-character) | A 64x64 top-down character with four directions, idle animation, and walk animation. | CC0 |
| [OpenGameArt — RPG character sprites](https://opengameart.org/content/rpg-character-sprites) | Character templates, directional sprites, walk cycles, and RPG character construction. | CC0 |
| [OpenGameArt — CC0 Characters](https://opengameart.org/content/cc0-characters) | Broad curated character collection for studying proportions, directions, and sprite consistency. | CC0 on tagged assets |

### Turnaround workflow

1. **Front view:** establish face, torso, limb placement, costume details, and proportions.
2. **Side view:** define head profile, spine curve, chest depth, hip position, and limb overlap.
3. **Back view:** resolve hair, cloak, backpack, armor plates, heels, and silhouette details.
4. **Three-quarter view:** connect front and side information without inventing new anatomy.
5. **Pixel pass:** simplify each view to the same visual density and palette.

### Side and back checklist

- Does the head, neck, and spine connect naturally?
- Are shoulders, hips, knees, and ankles aligned consistently?
- Does the back view explain details hidden from the front?
- Are accessories placed logically on every view?
- Does the silhouette remain readable at the target resolution?

## Secondary motion: cloth, flags, hair, and capes

| Resource | Best for | License / status |
|---|---|---|
| [OpenGameArt — Animated Flags Pack](https://opengameart.org/content/animated-flags-pack) | 458 CC0 animated flags with 16-frame wave animations, shaded and unshaded versions, plus a shading sprite sheet. | CC0 |
| [Lospec — Fabric / Flags tutorial](https://lospec.com/pixel-art-tutorials) | Focused guidance on pixel-art cloth movement, folds, and looping flag animation. | Check tutorial page |
| [Lospec — Pixel Art Tutorials](https://lospec.com/pixel-art-tutorials) | Broad tutorial index for animation timing, walk cycles, effects, cloth, and secondary motion. | Check tutorial page |
| [OpenGameArt — OPP2017](https://opengameart.org/content/opp2017-sprites-characters-objects-effects) | Large sprite and animation set including characters, animals, effects, particles, and UI elements. | Mixed; includes CC0 assets |

### Cloth animation principles

- **Follow-through:** A cape continues moving after the body stops.
- **Overlap:** Different parts of cloth move at different times.
- **Drag:** Loose fabric lags behind the character’s movement.
- **Anchor points:** Identify where cloth attaches—shoulders, waist, wrists, pole, or wall.
- **Fewer frames can be better:** A 4- or 6-frame loop often reads more cleanly than a overly smooth animation.

### Practice exercises

- Animate a 16x16 flag in a steady wind.
- Animate a cape during a walk cycle.
- Animate a skirt or robe during a turn.
- Animate hair blowing in wind.
- Animate a banner, curtain, or hanging cloth in an interior.

| [OpenGameArt — Tileset Pixel](https://opengameart.org/content/tileset-pixel) | CC0 pixel tileset for studying modular interior construction. | CC0 |
| [OpenGameArt — Tilesets and Backgrounds (PixelArt)](https://opengameart.org/content/tilesets-and-backgrounds-pixelart) | Pixel-art tilesets and background assets for rooms, buildings, and environmental scenes. | Mixed — check each asset |
| [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com/) | CC0 HDRIs, textures, materials, and 3D assets for realistic interior lighting and material studies. | CC0 |

### Interior design layers

| Layer | What to design |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Walls, floors, ceilings, doorways, windows, stairs, and structural details |
| Furniture | Beds, tables, chairs, shelves, cabinets, altars, workbenches, and storage |
| Props | Books, candles, food, tools, rugs, pottery, weapons, and personal objects |
| Lighting | Windows, fireplaces, lanterns, torches, magical light, and shadow direction |
| Storytelling | Ownership, profession, wealth, recent events, and hidden narrative clues |

### Interior readability checklist

- Does the room have a clear focal point?
- Can the viewer tell where entrances and walkable space are?
- Do wall and floor tiles transition cleanly?
- Is furniture scaled believably to the character?
- Does lighting establish time of day and mood?
- Do props reveal who lives or works in the space?

## Recommended starter set

1. **Art in Context Pose Reference** — public-domain/CC0 figure, action, and hand references  
2. **OpenGameArt Cartoon Male Turnaround** — complete CC0 character turnaround and walk cycle  
3. **OpenGameArt Animated Flags Pack** — CC0 cloth and flag secondary-motion reference  
4. **OpenGameArt CC0 Tiles & Tilesets** — interiors, dungeons, rooms, and modular environments  
5. **Poly Haven** — realistic lighting, materials, and interior rendering support  

---

## License notes

- **CC0** means “no rights reserved.” You may use, modify, redistribute, and commercialize tagged assets without attribution, though credit is courteous.
- **Art in Context** states that its pose references are public domain or CC0, with the artist, year, license, and source link shown beneath each image. [web:82]
- **OpenGameArt collections can mix licenses.** Verify the license on each individual asset page; OpenGameArt also cautions that automatically generated credit files may be inaccurate. [web:78]
- For production work, keep a license log with asset name, source URL, license, author, and download date.
